blocks.text: The start boundary defines the child range
At state `start = s`, each index i in [s, n) creates one child. That child appends candidates[i] and receives `start = i + 1`, so the chosen index and every earlier index are unavailable below it.

Considering the whole suffix is necessary for completeness: choosing only s + 1 would omit all other first choices. Restarting at zero or revisiting indices through s would allow reuse and reordered representations of the same combination.

A segment beginning at s is `[s, end)`. Nonemptiness requires `end > s`, and staying inside the string requires `end <= n`, so the raw candidate ends are s + 1, s + 2, ..., n.

Each boundary is then tested by the segment predicate. Omitting end = n loses the full remaining suffix; including end = s creates an empty segment that does not advance; boundaries before s revisit processed input.
For a nonempty half-open segment from s, enumerate every exclusive end in `(s, n]`.

blocks.text: Order is not membership

A collect-all search that visits every legal child from the same restored parent reaches the same valid leaves under any permutation of those children. Their emission order changes, but leaf validity does not.

Ordering can affect time to a first solution, cache behavior, or pruning opportunities whose proofs remain sound. It neither removes the need to undo mutation nor creates duplicates by itself; those depend on state restoration and identity rules.
Heuristics may reorder a complete child set; they may not silently remove legal children.

Duplicates arise from candidate identity and duplicate-control rules, not from permuting an otherwise correct loop.

blocks.text: Exhaustion is not completion

Two independent tests can stop a recursive call. The completion test asks whether the current path already satisfies the result contract. Candidate exhaustion asks whether this incomplete path has any legal child. Here completion is false and no child exists, so the branch is a dead end and contributes no result.

Returning from the call transfers control to its parent. The parent restores any state changed for this branch and continues with the next sibling candidate. Nothing about this local failure invalidates choices elsewhere in the search tree.

A valid result must pass the completion contract, which the prompt explicitly says this state does not. Restarting from the root would repeat work and discard the parent’s remaining siblings. Appending an empty result would record an object unrelated to the current incomplete path and violate the result contract.

blocks.text: Count the slots that still must be filled

A complete k-combination needs k values. After choosing c values, the branch still needs k - c values. The r remaining candidate positions can contribute at most r values, so completion requires r >= k - c.

If r < k - c, even selecting every remaining candidate leaves at least one slot empty. For example, if k = 5, c = 3, and r = 1, the branch needs two more values but can choose only one. No descendant can complete the combination, so enumeration can stop.

Equality is not a reason to stop: when r = k - c, the branch has exactly enough positions and may still succeed by choosing all of them. This capacity test proves impossibility; it is not a guess about which choices look promising.

r equaling the original input length usually describes the root and says nothing about insufficient capacity. c > 0 merely says the path is partial. r > 0 means a choice is available, not that enumeration should stop.

blocks.text: An occurrence can be part of the state

An index identifies an occurrence, while a value identifies only its payload. If equal values occupy positions 1 and 4, choosing index 1 and choosing index 4 are different state transitions whenever the problem contract distinguishes which input occurrence was used.

Index-based enumeration can therefore mark exactly one occurrence as used and later restore that mark. Enumerating by value alone would merge the two candidates before the solver has established that they are interchangeable.

If the output contract treats value-equal results as duplicates, a separate duplicate-control rule may skip equivalent sibling branches. That rule is applied deliberately after the candidate occurrences and the desired output identity are understood.

Equal values can be compared normally. Indices preserve positions but do not reorder the input. Choosing by index also does not remove mutable path state: a used-index mark still has to be undone before the next sibling.

blocks.text: Completeness needs coverage and branch isolation

items: Coverage: eventually consider every legal next choice. The only stated early exit is a find-one contract that has already found its required result.
Legality: exclude a choice before recursion only when the rules prove that it cannot belong to a valid child state.
Isolation: restore mutable state after each child so the next sibling starts from the same parent state.

blocks.text: Together these properties make the candidate loop represent the complete set of legal children of the current node. Missing a legal child loses every solution below it; retaining an illegal child breaks the state invariant; failing to restore state changes what later siblings mean.
A heuristic may reorder candidates to find useful branches earlier, but “looks promising” is not a correctness proof. Omitting an unpromising-looking legal choice can remove a valid solution.

blocks.text: Separate tree width from path depth

At the root, any of n values may fill the first position. After one choice, n - 1 values remain; then n - 2, down to one final choice. The number of complete leaves is therefore n × (n - 1) × ... × 1 = n!, so the leaves dimension is O(n!).

Along any one root-to-leaf path, exactly one position is filled per recursive level. A complete permutation contains n choices, so at most a linear number of calls are simultaneously active. Whether one counts n choice levels or n + 1 call frames including the root, the maximum recursion depth is O(n).

These answers do not claim the entire algorithm runs in only O(n!) time. If each emitted permutation is copied into an output collection, copying n values per leaf contributes O(n · n!) output work. The prompt asks only for leaf count and live recursion depth.

O(2^n) describes binary include/exclude leaves, not a branch factor that shrinks from n to 1. O(n^n) would allow every value at every position instead of removing used values. The factorial number of leaves does not make one path factorially deep.
